items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Having dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a bigger rise in sugar, with dinners at 8-9 pm linked to a rise about 13.3 mg/dL more than earlier ones. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference for you.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 12.6 hours, which is a good start, and some studies suggest that longer overnight fasts might be linked to smaller rises in sugar. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed some numbers, but it's still not clear if it makes a big difference.
